skill.name: twitter-automation
skill.description: Use inference.sh belt CLI recipes to run Twitter/X actions such as posting, media publishing, likes, retweets, DMs, follows, deletes, and profile lookups.
skill.summary: Run Twitter/X automation workflows through inference.sh belt CLI commands.
skill.author: inference-sh-skills

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command matches are Markdown code fences or inline app IDs, but several examples do instruct users or agents to run belt and npx commands with real network and account side effects. The highest contextual concern is that the skill enables posting, DMs, follows, likes, retweets, and deletes without visible consent or rate-limit safeguards. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed SKILL.md content.

remediation.issue: External CLI and skill installation commands
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running belt or npx commands, and pin installation instructions to trusted, immutable sources when possible.
Add clear safeguards for consent, rate limits, account ownership, and human review before likes, retweets, follows, DMs, posts, or deletes are executed.

remediation.issue: Remote media and mutable documentation links
remediation.suggestion: Use trusted official domains, avoid mutable install URLs for security-sensitive setup, and disclose that rendered images or links may load external resources.
Mark delete, publish, DM, follow, like, and retweet workflows as approval-gated actions in the skill instructions.

content.value_statement: Teams need repeatable ways to run Twitter/X actions without rebuilding integration steps. This skill provides belt CLI recipes for posting, media publishing, engagement, DMs, follows, deletes, and profile lookups.
actual_capabilities: Provides belt CLI commands for Twitter/X authentication and app execution.
Shows how to post text updates and create media posts.
Includes examples for likes, retweets, post deletion, and post lookup.
Includes examples for sending DMs, following users, and reading user profiles.
Shows workflows that generate images or videos before publishing them to Twitter/X.
limitations: Requires the belt CLI, an inference.sh account, and a configured Twitter/X integration.
Does not include its own scheduler, application code, or automated retry system.
Does not add consent checks, moderation checks, or rate limiting by itself.
Twitter/X API permissions, quotas, and platform rules may limit available actions.

use_cases.title: Publish Approved Updates
use_cases.description: Prepare and run repeatable posting commands for approved text or media updates.

use_cases.title: Share Launch Assets
use_cases.description: Generate image or video assets and publish them through a connected Twitter/X account.

use_cases.title: Manage Account Interactions
use_cases.description: Retrieve posts or profiles and run approved follow, DM, like, or retweet actions.

prompt_templates.title: Post a Text Update
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare a safe belt command to post this approved Twitter/X update: [paste text]. Ask before running anything.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Media Post
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Twitter/X media post workflow using this approved text and media URL. Include a review step before publishing.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Engagement Action
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether this planned like, retweet, follow, or DM action is appropriate. Then prepare the belt command only if it passes review.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Campaign Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a human-approved Twitter/X workflow for a launch campaign using posts, media, profile lookups, and engagement actions. Include approval checkpoints and rate limits.

output_examples.input: Post an approved product update to Twitter/X.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks for final approval, confirms the connected account, prepares the posting step, and reports the resulting post link after execution.

output_examples.input: Publish an approved image with a short caption.
output_examples.output: The assistant verifies the media URL, checks the caption, prepares a media post workflow, and waits for approval before publishing.

output_examples.input: Send a thank-you DM to a known customer.
output_examples.output: The assistant verifies recipient consent and account ownership, prepares the message action, and asks for confirmation before sending.

best_practices: Get human approval before publishing, deleting, liking, retweeting, following, or sending DMs.
Review generated text and media for accuracy, rights, privacy, and platform-policy compliance.
Keep credentials out of prompts and use the minimum account permissions needed.
anti_patterns: Running bulk follow, like, retweet, or DM loops for audience growth without consent.
Publishing AI-generated media without reviewing rights, accuracy, or disclosure needs.
Allowing an agent to delete posts or publish public content without explicit approval.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It provides belt CLI recipes for Twitter/X posting, media posts, likes, retweets, DMs, follows, deletes, and lookups.

faq.question: Does it require a Twitter/X integration?
faq.answer: Yes. You need the belt CLI, an inference.sh account, and a connected Twitter/X integration.

faq.question: Can it schedule posts by itself?
faq.answer: No. The skill shows command workflows, but it does not include a scheduler.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when the required CLI is available.

faq.question: Is it safe to run engagement actions automatically?
faq.answer: No. Use human approval, consent checks, and rate limits before likes, retweets, follows, or DMs.

faq.question: Does it manage API credentials?
faq.answer: No. Authentication is handled through the belt CLI and the connected inference.sh account.
